# `@warlock.js/devtools` — overview

A dashboard served by your own app. In **development** it lives at `/__warlock`
and answers loopback clients only. In **production** it is an opt-in monitor at
a secret path (see "Production monitor" below). It shows what each request did:
its timing waterfall, the queries it ran, the cache operations, the logs, and
any mail it sent, plus query and route statistics, errors, resources, health
and jobs. The dashboard is a React app; panel view modules work as before.

## Install: one command, no config

```bash
warlock add devtools   # adds @warlock.js/devtools as a DEV dependency
warlock dev            # open http://localhost:<port>/__warlock
```

There's nothing to register. `warlock dev` loads devtools automatically when
the package is installed.

For development only, do not add `devtoolsConnector()` to `warlock.config.ts`:
it is a dev dependency, so a production install doesn't have it. For the
production monitor you do add it, as a regular dependency (next sections).

## Why it can't leak into production

1. **It isn't installed there.** Production installs omit dev dependencies.
2. **It refuses to run outside development.** If it's present anyway, it logs
   one warning (`@warlock.js/devtools only runs in development; it is not mounted`)
   and mounts nothing.
3. **It only answers loopback clients.** Every dashboard and API route answers
   404 unless the connection comes from `127.0.0.1` / `::1`. It checks the
   socket address, not `X-Forwarded-For`, so a forwarded-for header can't
   unlock it.
4. **It only answers loopback hosts.** The `Host` must be `localhost`,
   `*.localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, a present `Origin` must be one of
   those, and a request carrying `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Host` /
   `X-Real-IP` / `Forwarded` (a local proxy or tunnel) is refused. This stops a
   website re-pointing its domain at 127.0.0.1 from reading request history,
   queries and mail. Each refusal reason is logged once in the terminal.

For a custom dev hostname or a private local proxy, add `src/config/devtools.ts`
(a plain object, safe in production):

```ts
export default {
  allowedHosts: ["app.test"], // default []; ".app.test" also matches subdomains
  allowProxied: false, // default false
};
```

## What each panel shows

| Panel                          | What you see                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Where it comes from                                           |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Requests**                   | Each request with its status, duration and query count. Click one for a waterfall: router middleware, `page.middleware`, loaders, `page.cache` hit/miss, `render.shell`, `defer.settle`, with queries and cache ops placed on the same time axis. | core `registerTracingHooks()`                                 |
| **Queries**                    | SQL + bindings or the Mongo command, duration, rows, and an **Explain** button (Postgres `SELECT` only; runs `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`, never `ANALYZE`)                                                                                            | cascade `dataSourceRegistry.on("query")`                      |
| **N+1**                        | `⚠ N+1: 12× "select … where post_id = $1" — src/app/posts/services/list-posts.service.ts:18`, shown on the request and printed in the terminal                                                                                                    | same query shape ≥ 5 times in one request                     |
| **Mail**                       | Every mail sent in development: headers, HTML (sandboxed) and text, attachment names                                                                                                                                                              | core `mailEvents.onCaptured()`                                |
| **Logs**                       | Log entries per request, filterable by level and module                                                                                                                                                                                           | a logger channel                                              |
| **Cache**                      | hit / miss / set / removed / `invalidated` (tags, keys removed)                                                                                                                                                                                   | cache `cache.on(...)`                                         |
| **Resources**                  | Memory, CPU, event-loop delay and garbage collection, with a 10-minute history                                                                                                                                                                    | the process                                                   |
| **Health**                     | Readiness checks over time                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | core `health.readiness()`                                     |
| **Errors**                     | Failed requests grouped by cause with counts                                                                                                                                                                                                      | tracing and logger                                            |
| **Jobs**                       | Registered scheduled jobs with schedule, last and next run (no run history, duration or error yet); queue counts only when the queue driver reports them (not available today)                                                                    | `@warlock.js/scheduler`, `@warlock.js/queue`                  |
| **AI Reports, Models, Errors** | Hourly totals of agent runs, tokens, estimated cost (from model pricing; unpriced models flagged), errors by category, latency, fallbacks and refusals, with 24h / 7d / 30d / custom ranges and Agent, Model, Provider filters. Production too    | `@warlock.js/ai-panoptic` trace feed, saved as hourly rollups |
| **AI Runs, Evaluate**          | Single runs with filters, grouping and a cost tint; grade a system prompt with a judge model. Development only                                                                                                                                    | Panoptic traces in memory; `panoptic.evaluate`                |
| **Agents**                     | Per-turn traces of `@warlock.js/ai` agents: system prompt, tools offered with schema hashes, tool calls, results and refusals, retries, usage and cost, plus a comparison with the previous run of the agent                                      | `@warlock.js/ai` `agentTraces` store                          |
| **Routes**                     | Every HTTP route with its method, path, name and middleware                                                                                                                                                                                       | core router                                                   |
| **API**                        | The app's API reference: every route with its parameters, request body, responses and auth                                                                                                                                                        | core `getDevelopmentOpenApiDocument()`                        |

Work outside a request (boot, scheduler ticks, queue jobs) goes to a separate
background list, so it never clutters a request's timeline.

## Request history survives restarts

With core's request log on (the default in development, `http.logging.requests`),
the **Requests** panel also reads `storage/logs/requests/*.jsonl`: history past
a restart and past the 200-request ring buffer, merged with live requests
without duplicates by id (saved-only rows are marked **saved**).

- Filter: `GET /__warlock/api/requests?status=5xx&route=posts&method=POST&since=1h&until=…&q=text&limit=50`
  (`status` is `404` or a class like `5xx`; `since` is a duration or ISO date).
  A bad value answers 400.
- Detail: `GET /__warlock/api/requests/:id` returns the in-memory request, or a
  saved one rebuilt from the log; either carries `record` (the full
  `RequestLogRecord`: redacted headers/body, response, error with stack, logs,
  query summary) when one was written. Per-query detail and Explain exist only
  for requests still in memory.
- Copy as curl: `GET /__warlock/api/requests/:id/curl` returns `{ curl }`;
  redacted values stay `[REDACTED]`.

An older core without the request log leaves the panel in-memory only.

## AI section: Reports, Runs, Agents, Models, Errors, Evaluate

The **AI** sidebar group has six pages. Reports (`ai-reports`), Models (`ai-models`) and Errors (`ai-errors`) read
**hourly rollups** (names and numbers only: agent, model, provider, runs, tokens, estimated cost, errors by category,
latency histogram, fallback and refusal counts). Runs (`ai`, id unchanged), Agents (`agents`) and Evaluate
(`ai-evaluate`) read in-memory data and exist in development only. Cost is always "Estimated from model pricing"; runs of
models without pricing are counted as unpriced and shown next to every cost (a model priced at 0 counts as priced).
Runs filters by text, status, type and exact HTTP request id (`GET api/ai/runs?requestId=`). A comparison whose
previous period is older than the kept history reads "No earlier data". Custom ranges longer than 8 days use daily
columns from local midnight to midnight.

Options in `src/config/devtools.ts`:

```ts
export default {
  ai: {
    reports: true, // keep hourly totals; false turns the writer off (pages say so)
    retentionDays: 30, // 1 to 400; default 30 in development, 90 in production
    flushIntervalMs: 60_000, // at least 5000
  },
};
```

- Storage: development files under `storage/devtools/ai-rollups`; production table `devtools_ai_rollups`, part of
  `devtoolsMigrations`. After upgrading run `warlock migrate`; without it one warning is logged and the pages answer
  `table-missing` ("AI reports need their table", command `warlock migrate`).
- Production tabs: Reports, Models and Errors are on by default when Panoptic is installed and loads; Runs, Agents and
  Evaluate stay off. `production.panels` overrides by id (`{ "ai-reports": false }`). Every process that boots the
  connector writes to the same table, so totals add up all instances and workers.
- Needs Panoptic and observation (`ai.config({ panoptic: { observeAll: true } })`). Evaluate also needs
  `ai.config({ panoptic: { evaluate: { model, instructions? } } })`; without it the page shows the setup.
- Routes: `GET /api/ai/reports`, `/api/ai/models`, `/api/ai/errors` (query `range=24h|7d|30d|custom`, `from`, `to`, `tz`,
  `agent`, `model`, `provider`), `GET /api/ai/runs` (`q`, `status`, `type`, `session`, `prompt`, `groupBy`, `limit`),
  `GET` and `POST /api/ai/evaluate`; `GET /api/ai`, `/api/ai/runs/:id` and `/api/ai/agent-runs*` keep their shapes. Error
  codes: `ai.range-invalid`, `ai.evaluate-unavailable`, `ai.prompt-not-found`, `ai.evaluate-failed`.
- Inside a Warlock app Panoptic's standalone dashboard does not start (one notice points here); the AI section replaces it.

## AI runs alongside HTTP requests

The **AI** tab and each request's **AI runs** section display completed traces
from optional `@warlock.js/ai-panoptic`. If the tab is empty it says why
(`/api/ai` answers `reason`: `ai-missing`, `panoptic-missing`, `panoptic-failed` with the load
error (absolute paths replaced) and versions, `observation-off`, or `table-missing`, `reports-off`, or `not-collected` in the
production dashboard, which keeps hourly totals but not single runs) with a title, one line and a copyable command; the
other panels keep working.

```bash
warlock add devtools
npm install @warlock.js/ai @warlock.js/ai-panoptic
```

At app boot, enable observation, then restart `warlock dev`:

```ts
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import "@warlock.js/ai-panoptic";
ai.config({ panoptic: { observeAll: true } });
```

No `dashboard: true` or extra listener port is needed. Existing `attach`,
middleware and explicit collection through Panoptic's built-in collector also
feed the panel. An installed but unobserved flow produces no trace.

- `DevtoolsAiRun` and `DevtoolsAiEvent` are public types from
  `@warlock.js/devtools`; `DevtoolsStreamEvent` includes the `ai` event.
- Read all runs with `GET /__warlock/api/ai`, or filter by an exact HTTP id with
  `GET /__warlock/api/ai?requestId=<encoded-id>`. Responses include `available`,
  `runs` and a root-usage `aggregate`; unavailable responses contain `message`.
- Inspect tools/timings, retry attempts and compaction records with
  `GET /__warlock/api/ai/runs/<encoded-trace-id>` (404 when evicted). The existing
  stream emits `ai` events with `{ traceId, requestId? }`.
- Model, input/output/cache-read/cache-write tokens and historical USD cost come
  from the trace, never a guessed price table. Unknown cost is unpriced. Root
  usage includes children already; do not sum all spans for a run total.
- Cache hits count trips reporting positive provider `cachedTokens`.
  Semantic-cache hits have no explicit report flag and remain unreported; zero
  tokens alone do not prove a hit. `—` means unreported rather than zero.
- `incomplete` status or normalized `AGENT_INCOMPLETE` / `AgentIncompleteError`
  marks truncation. Recovered truncated trips still contribute to their count.
- Compaction metadata includes applied/skipped agent decisions and provider
  compaction-block counts; summary content is omitted. Orchestrator result-only
  compaction cannot be reconstructed from a report-only trace.

### Agent traces

The **Agents** tab needs no Panoptic: `@warlock.js/ai` 5.38+ records a trace per
agent run in development and devtools reads its shared store. Endpoints:
`GET /__warlock/api/ai/agent-runs[?requestId=<id>]` (list, newest first; `available:
false` with guidance until the AI package has created its store),
`GET /__warlock/api/ai/agent-runs/<run-id>` (full trace, 404 when evicted), and
`agent-trace` events `{ runId, status, requestId? }` on the stream. Unlike the
Panoptic view these carry prompt and tool content (secret keys are redacted
before storage), so they stay behind the same development and loopback guard.
`warlock ai trace [runId] [--diff other]` prints the same data. Public types:
`DevtoolsAgentRun`, `DevtoolsAgentTraceEvent`.

A same-origin browser tool can consume the public types directly:

```ts
import type { DevtoolsAiEvent, DevtoolsAiRun, DevtoolsStreamEvent } from "@warlock.js/devtools";

const response = await fetch("/__warlock/api/ai?requestId=request-42");
const { runs }: { runs: DevtoolsAiRun[] } = await response.json();
console.log(runs.map((run) => [run.traceId, run.usage, run.cost]));

function handleStream(event: DevtoolsStreamEvent): void {
  if (event.type === "ai") {
    const update: DevtoolsAiEvent = event.data;
    console.log(update.traceId, update.requestId);
  }
}
handleStream({ type: "ai", data: { traceId: "run-42", requestId: "request-42" } });
```

Request correlation reads core's current request id at collection time, before
exporters. Concurrent/late runs can retain their async context. No id means
background; `sessionId` is never substituted. Replayed reports outside the
request cannot recover its context automatically.

Devtools retains its own content-free in-memory store, at most `maxRequests`
traces (200 by default), independently of HTTP request retention. Clear/shutdown
empties this view, leaving application exporter/cache stores alone. Boot-time
and persisted traces are not replayed. The source only attaches in development;
AI routes keep the same socket-loopback guard as every other panel.

## API docs

`/__warlock/docs` renders the app's OpenAPI 3.1 document with [Scalar](https://github.com/scalar/scalar); the dashboard's **API** tab shows the same page and has a **Scalar | Swagger UI** switch (remembered in the browser). `/__warlock/docs/swagger` renders the same document with [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). The document comes from `GET /__warlock/api/openapi.json`, built in-process by core's `getDevelopmentOpenApiDocument()` from the routes already registered, so it is the same generator as `warlock generate.openapi` and follows your edits with no CLI run. It covers API routes (not pages): paths, parameters, request bodies from Seal validation, responses from each handler's `responseSchema`, `401`/`422` and bearer/cookie security from `authMiddleware()`. See core's `generate-openapi` topic for what is documented and how to declare it.

- It answers `503` from `/__warlock/api/openapi.json` when the host provides no generator.
- Same guard as the rest of devtools: dev-only and loopback-only.
- Scalar's prebuilt bundle is vendored and served as `assets/scalar.js`, so apps install nothing extra. The page fetches nothing from a CDN, and Scalar's web fonts, telemetry, AI agent and MCP are turned off.
- Swagger UI's prebuilt bundle (swagger-ui-dist, Apache-2.0) is vendored too, served as `assets/swagger-ui-bundle.js` and `assets/swagger-ui.css`; its schema validator badge is off, so it fetches nothing from outside either.
- The API tab links `OpenAPI JSON` (`/__warlock/api/openapi.json`) and `Postman collection` (`/__warlock/api/postman.json`, built by core's `getDevelopmentPostmanCollection()`; `503` when core cannot build one) for importing the routes into Postman or Insomnia.
- To write a file instead, run `warlock generate.openapi` (default `storage/openapi/openapi.json`).

## Options

`warlock dev` uses the defaults: path `/__warlock`, the last 200 requests
kept, and an N+1 threshold of 5. Everything lives in memory and is gone on
restart.

## From the terminal (agents)

`npx warlock trace POST /posts --body '{"title":"Hi"}' --json` sends one
request to the running dev server and prints this dashboard's record of it as
JSON — middleware, validation result, queries with N+1 flags, logs, response
and timings. See the `warlock-trace` skill of `@warlock.js/core`.

`npx warlock mcp` (or `npx warlock dev --mcp`) gives a coding agent the same
records through its `requests_recent` tool: the newest requests with their
phases, queries flagged `nPlusOne`, warnings, logs and timings. See the
`warlock-mcp` skill of `@warlock.js/core`.

## Secrets

Query bindings and log context go through the logger's redaction rules
before they're stored. The data is still real request data, which is exactly
why the development dashboard is loopback-only. The production monitor removes
values before storing anything (see "Production monitor").

## Related

- Building your own tooling on the same hooks: core `registerTracingHooks()`,
  cascade `dataSourceRegistry.on("query")`, core `mailEvents.onCaptured()` and
  the cache `invalidated` event are public APIs that also work without devtools.

## Process supervision panel

Run `npx warlock add process` to create an app-owned supervisor and
`src/app/processes/devtools.ts`, exporting `processPanel = { list: () =>
processes.list() }`. Devtools discovers this registration only in development.
The **Processes** tab refreshes `GET /__warlock/api/processes`: PIDs, workload
categories, labels, display commands, limits, enforcement, and peak memory.
It excludes ownership tokens. Without registration the list is empty. The
endpoint retains development/loopback guards and provides no stop action.
Use the `warlock-js-process` skill for launch,
recovery and stop APIs; configure one owner/registry per application instance.

## Production monitor

Opt in: nothing is mounted or captured in production unless
`production.enabled` is `true`. Install the package as a regular dependency,
then register it in `warlock.config.ts`. `@warlock.js/devtools/production`
exports `devtoolsMigrations` and `registerDevtoolsCommands`, which adds the
`devtools:enable` and `devtools:reset-admin` commands.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@warlock.js/core";
import { devtoolsConnector } from "@warlock.js/devtools";
import { devtoolsMigrations, registerDevtoolsCommands } from "@warlock.js/devtools/production";

export default defineConfig({
  connectors: [devtoolsConnector()],
  cli: { commands: [registerDevtoolsCommands()] },
  database: { migrations: [...devtoolsMigrations] },
});
```

Then run `warlock migrate`, and enable it in `src/config/devtools.ts`:

```ts
export default {
  panels: ["@warlock.js/grimoire/devtools"],
  production: {
    enabled: true,
    trustedProxies: ["loopback"],
    sampleRate: 0.1,
  },
};
```

Environment variables:

- `DEVTOOLS_PATH`: the secret dashboard path (`/ops-7f3k2q9x`; at least 8 characters, never `/__warlock`).
- `DEVTOOLS_ADMIN_EMAIL` with `DEVTOOLS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (changed at first sign-in) or `DEVTOOLS_SETUP_TOKEN` (32+ characters; the admin opens `<origin><path>/#/setup/<token>`). Not both.
- `encryption.key` (64 hex characters) must be set in `src/config/encryption.ts`.

The accounts live in the app's database through Cascade. Roles are `viewer`
and `admin`. Admins invite users with a 24-hour single-use link. Two-factor is
required for admins by default (`twoFactor: "admins"`; or `"everyone"`, or `"off"` for nobody, which logs a boot warning; an account that has a factor is always asked for it): an
authenticator app, or passkeys when `@simplewebauthn/server` is installed, plus
10 recovery codes. Every closed case answers the app's own 404.

Options under `production` (all optional, defaults in brackets):
`enabled` [false], `path` [`DEVTOOLS_PATH`], `sampleRate` [0.1],
`slowRequestMs` [1000], `slowQueryMs` [200], `maxRequests` [200],
`requestRetentionHours` [24], `maxStoredSamplesPerMinute` [120],
`reportIntervalMs` [10000], `trustedProxies` [[]], `requireHttps` [true],
`allowedIps` [[]], `origin`, `session.idleMinutes` [30], `session.maxHours` [8],
`twoFactor` ["admins"], `passwords.minLength` [8, from 8 to 72], `passwords.rejectCommon` [true], `rateLimits.windowMinutes` [15], `rateLimits.account`
[5], `rateLimits.ip` [20], `rateLimits.global` [100], `rateLimits.lockMinutes`
[15], `explain.executing` [false], `panels` [{}], `logLevels` [warn, error],
`auditRetentionDays` [90], `passkeys.rpName`, `passkeys.rpId`.

- Redaction: queries are stored as their shape (no literals or bindings), logs
  lose `context`, phases lose `attrs`, cache keys become counts, request error
  messages and stacks, and error-level log lines, lose quoted values, emails and `{ … }` documents, headers
  and bodies come only from core's request log. Paths are kept (no query
  string): keep secrets out of URL paths.
- EXPLAIN is admin-only and plain (`EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`, MongoDB
  `queryPlanner`), for one read statement only (a MongoDB aggregate with `$out`
  or `$merge` never). PostgreSQL plans run in a read-only transaction that is
  rolled back. `explain.executing: true` allows `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` and
  `executionStats`; they run the query, so leave it off unless accepted.
  Production plans show `?` in place of the query's values.
- MongoDB: with `devtools.production.enabled` in `src/config/devtools.ts`, core
  turns `queryEvents` on in processes that serve HTTP (command monitoring is off
  in production by default); an explicit `queryEvents: false` wins. With the
  option passed only to `devtoolsConnector()`, set `queryEvents: true` yourself.
- A correct password does not reset an account's failed-try count; only a
  completed sign-in (second factor included) does. A caller over the IP limit
  costs no password check, and refused tries are audited at most once a minute
  per address and account. The per-IP limit counts an IPv6 client by its /64
  (an IPv4-mapped address as its IPv4 address).
- From the account page, adding or removing a second factor needs the current
  password (`current` in the JSON body, also on `DELETE api/account/totp` and
  `DELETE api/account/passkeys/:id`); removing also accepts a passkey check
  from the last five minutes. New recovery codes need a TOTP code or that
  passkey check, which is single use.
- Several instances share the database: each writes a report every 10 s, the
  instance picker filters, the live stream is per instance.
- Disable from the dashboard (admin); re-enable with `warlock devtools:enable`
  or a new `DEVTOOLS_PATH`. Lost admin: `warlock devtools:reset-admin --email <email>`.
- Behind a proxy set `trustedProxies`, set `origin`, and have the proxy set
  (not pass through) `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Proto` and
  `X-Forwarded-Host`; turn off proxy buffering (or rely on
  `X-Accel-Buffering: no`) for the live view.
- Tabs on in production: requests, queries, routes, resources, health, errors,
  logs, jobs. `mail`, `ai`, `agents`, `api`, `processes` need
  `panels: { id: true }`. A package panel needs `production: true` or the same.
- Panel writes in production need an admin and the `X-Devtools-Csrf` header
  (`api()` adds it); they are audited.
- Share links: `production.share = { enabled: true, maxDays: 30 }` lets an
  admin (Admin, Share links) give a read-only link to one panel that declares
  `share`. The table `devtools_shares` is in `devtoolsMigrations` (`DT008`
  names it when `share.enabled` and it is missing; `maxDays` is 1 to 365 or
  `DT007`). The URL is `<origin><path>/#/share/<token>`: the token is in the
  fragment, shown once, stored only as a SHA-256 hash, and the page removes it
  from the address bar. Opening it sets the cookie `__Secure-warlock-devtools-share`
  (at most 12 hours, HMAC-signed) that reaches only that panel's `share.routes`,
  `share.assets` and images. A wrong, expired or revoked token, a bad cookie and
  sharing being off all answer the uniform 404; a failed token is audited as
  `share.failed` (counts toward `rateLimits.ip`); `share.created` and
  `share.revoked` are audited too. A revoke reaches every instance within 5 s.
  Not available in development. Tell people not to put the link in tickets or
  chat they do not trust: anyone holding it can read the shared view.

### When something fails

The app refuses to boot with a `DevtoolsProductionConfigError`
(`DEVTOOLS_CONFIG_CODES` holds the messages):

| Code    | Fix                                                                                                                                                |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DT001` | Set `DEVTOOLS_PATH` or `production.path`.                                                                                                          |
| `DT002` | Use a path of 8+ characters starting with `/`, with letters, digits and `- _ . ~ /` only; not `/__warlock`.                                        |
| `DT003` | No admin: set `DEVTOOLS_ADMIN_EMAIL` plus a password or setup token, or run `warlock devtools:reset-admin --email <email>`.                        |
| `DT004` | The env password breaks the rules (`passwords.minLength`+ characters, at most 72 bytes, not common unless `rejectCommon` is false, not the email). |
| `DT005` | Install `@warlock.js/cascade` and configure a database.                                                                                            |
| `DT006` | Set `encryption.key` (64 hex characters).                                                                                                          |
| `DT007` | An option is invalid (`share.maxDays` must be 1 to 365); the message names it.                                                                     |
| `DT008` | Add `devtoolsMigrations` to `database.migrations` and run `warlock migrate` (`devtools_shares` when sharing is on).                                |
| `DT009` | Set the password or the setup token, not both.                                                                                                     |
| `DT010` | The setup token needs 32+ characters (`openssl rand -base64 32`).                                                                                  |

Every dashboard URL gives a 404: check that `production.enabled` is true, the
dashboard is not disabled or locked (`warlock devtools:enable`), the request is
HTTPS (`trustedProxies`), the IP is in `allowedIps`, the tab is not turned off,
and you opened the exact `DEVTOOLS_PATH`. Most closed cases log nothing on
purpose. The boot line `devtools production monitor mounted at /ops-… (DEVTOOLS_PATH)`
shows the monitor started; the audit log has `dashboard.disabled`,
`dashboard.locked` and `login.blocked`; only an unreadable state or session
store logs a warning (`devtools`, at most once a minute).

Full pages: "Devtools in production" and "Devtools security" in the docs.

## Registering a panel

A package or the app adds a tab with one line in `src/config/devtools.ts`:

```ts
export default {
  panels: ["@acme/queue/devtools"], // or "./src/devtools/queue-panel.ts"
  // pass options to a panel factory (root and mode always win): [["@acme/queue/devtools", { pageSize: 50 }]]
};
```

Devtools imports each entry only in development (a package export resolves
from the app root, a `./` path is relative to it). The module's default export
is a `DevtoolsPanelExport`: a `DevtoolsPanel`, a list, or a function (sync or
async) receiving `{ root }` that returns either. Use `import type` so the
module never needs devtools at runtime.

```ts
import type { DevtoolsPanelExport } from "@warlock.js/devtools";

const queuePanel: DevtoolsPanelExport = ({ root }) => ({
  id: "queue", // lower-case letters, digits, dashes
  title: "Queue", // the tab label
  view: new URL("./queue-view.js", import.meta.url), // served at /__warlock/panels/queue/view.js
  assets: { "chart.js": new URL("./queue-chart.js", import.meta.url) }, // /__warlock/panels/queue/chart.js
  routes: [
    { path: "", handler: () => ({ root, jobs: [] }) }, // GET /__warlock/api/queue
    { path: "/jobs/:id", handler: ({ params }) => ({ id: params.id }) },
    { method: "POST", path: "/retry", handler: ({ body }) => ({ retried: body }) },
  ],
});

export default queuePanel;
```

- A handler (`DevtoolsPanelRoute`) receives a `DevtoolsPanelRequest`
  (`{ params, query, body }`); its return value is sent as JSON with
  `Cache-Control: no-store`, `undefined` sends `204`, and a thrown error with a
  `statusCode` answers that status with `{ error: message }`.
- The view module is browser JavaScript. Its default export receives
  `{ id, root, api, route, href, navigate, refresh, asset, el, svg, empty }`
  and fills `root` or returns an element. `api("search?q=a")` fetches
  `api/<id>/search?q=a` as JSON; `href("jobs/7")` is `#queue/jobs/7`, a link
  that opens that view (`route` is then `"jobs/7"`); `svg()` builds SVG
  elements for small graphs. Build text with `text`, never `innerHTML`.
- Every panel route, view and asset sits behind the devtools guard
  (in development: loopback socket and host, no foreign `Origin`, no proxy
  headers; in production: sign-in). A reused id (the built-in `processes` included) or a dashboard id
  such as `mail` is refused; devtools logs why and leaves the panel out.

- `files: { dir, extensions? }` serves a folder of images at
  `/__warlock/panels/<id>/files/<path>` (default `.png .jpg .jpeg .webp .gif`;
  `.svg`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.js` and `.mjs` are refused when the panel loads;
  `..`, backslashes, absolute paths and links that leave the folder answer
  404). The view builds the URL with `file("login/step-1.png")`.
- `share: { view, routes, assets?, files? }` (`DevtoolsPanelShare`) declares
  the view a read-only share link opens. `routes` are paths of the panel's GET
  routes; each such route gets `shared: true` in its `DevtoolsPanelRequest`
  and must leave file paths, code, test names and error messages out of its
  answer. The view context also has `shared` and `share` (`{ enabled,
  manageHref }` for an admin when sharing is on, else `null`).
- The factory also receives `errors()`: the captured error groups of the last
  hour as `DevtoolsPanelErrorSummary[]` (route, status, class name, source,
  count, first and last seen; no message, no stack; every instance in
  production). Call it per request.

A panel can set `production: true` when it is safe in the production monitor
(otherwise it needs `production.panels[id]: true`). The factory receives
`{ root, mode, errors }`; `mode` is `"development"` or `"production"`, and a panel must
not write files in production. The ids `resources`, `health`, `errors`, `jobs`,
`instances`, `auth`, `account`, `admin` and `share` are reserved.

Full reference: the "Registering a panel" page of the devtools docs.

Panel styling: a package panel's CSS may use only the dashboard's variables (`DEVTOOLS_PANEL_TOKENS`, exported by
`@warlock.js/devtools`: `--background --foreground --card --muted --muted-foreground --accent --border --brand
--success --warning --info --destructive --chart-1..5` and the other shadcn names) plus variables it defines itself.
Never use another name (such as `--text` or `--surface`): the dashboard does not define it, and text can become
unreadable. The text tokens meet 4.5:1 contrast on `--background` and `--card` in both themes. In the light theme `--primary` is the
gold fill (dark `--primary-foreground` on it) and `--brand` is the deep amber for text; in the dark theme both are gold.

The dashboard shows the Warlock logo and installed core version at the top of the sidebar and the app's own
`package.json` name and version at the bottom. They come from `GET api/auth/session` (`warlockVersion`, `app`), read once
on the server, signed-in only, `null` when unknown.
